LESSON: LETTER SOUNDS AND LETTER NAMES-PHONICS

Grade: Grade 1
Subject: LITERACY ACTIVITIES
Strand: WRITING
Topic 4.1: Letter Sounds and letter names-Phonics

SECTION 1: WELCOME

• Today’s class: Letter Sounds and letter names-Phonics
• How we learn: Teach → Worked example → Try this
• Use point notes. Show working. Then take the quiz.
• Big question: How are words letter names-Phonics the learner should be able to: (unique to the indigenous languages) formed?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

1. write upper and lower case  Learners sound diagraphs and words with 3 lessons letters correctly consonant clusters(ng, dh etc.)

SECTION 3: CLASS STUDY (TEACH → EXAMPLE → TRY)

▸ Letter Sounds and letter names-Phonics

• Listen to a model.
• Study the example.
• Then produce your own example.

▸ Letter Sounds and letter names-Phonics

Teach
• Focus skill: write upper and lower case  Learners sound diagraphs and words with 3 lessons letters correctly consonant clusters(ng, dh etc.).
• Use complete sentences.
• Speak clearly; write neatly.

Worked example
• Model sentence 1 about Letter Sounds and letter names-Phonics.
• Model sentence 2 using a Kenyan school example.
• Model dialogue: A: “…?”  B: “…”

Try this
• Write 5 original sentences on this skill.
• Say one 30-second oral example to a partner.


SECTION: QUICK EXAMPLES

• One clear model for Letter Sounds and letter names-Phonics
• One Kenyan school/home example

SECTION: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences.
2. Do one oral practice with a partner.
3. Correct spelling/punctuation.

SECTION: WORK TO DO

1. Revision sheet: meaning + 5 examples + 5 practice items.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How are words letter names-Phonics the learner should be able to: (unique to the indigenous languages) formed?

SECTION: REMEMBER

• Model first, then try.
• Use complete sentences.

• Next: complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Classroom study notes (Strategy 2)
